POLI-LUNAR is an interactive educational web application designed to help students explore the objects that NASA has left in space. It provides information and images about space objects, including those located on the Moon, Mars, and beyond. The application features POLI, a reading assistant that helps users understand the content, interactive tutorials, and a 12-question quiz to test their knowledge. POLI-LUNAR works on computers and mobile devices and can also be installed as an application on compatible smartphones. Its main goal is to make learning about space exploration more accessible, interesting, and fun for everyone.

POLI-LUNAR – Project Description
POLI-LUNAR is an interactive educational web application that helps people learn about the objects NASA has left in space, including the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Users can explore information and images, follow tutorials, listen to content with POLI, a reading assistant, and answer a 12-question quiz to test their knowledge.
The main benefits of this project are making space science easier to understand, encouraging curiosity, and providing an interactive way to learn. Its intended impact is to help students and other users discover more about space exploration in an entertaining and accessible way.
We developed POLI-LUNAR using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. We used GitHub to store and publish the project, and GitHub Pages to make it available online. We worked with a laptop and a mobile phone to develop and test the application.
The creative aspect of POLI-LUNAR is the combination of space exploration, educational content, an assistant named POLI, and interactive activities in one place. We considered accessibility, ease of use, compatibility with different devices, and making learning fun.
Our goal is to bring the wonders of space closer to everyone.
